page.description: Gentoo Linux minimal install image: size, checksum and a licensed screenshot.
page.intro: A source-based distribution built around Portage. This is the minimal install image: it boots, enters a shell and hands the build to you.
pros: You choose the USE flags, profile and init, then rebuild what matters.
A running system can be trimmed to exactly what it needs.
cons: Compiling takes real time; the minimal image builds the system.
Rolling updates need attention, especially with a custom profile.
The install image is 1 GB and has no desktop.
The Commons screenshot is from 2008, not this build.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of Gentoo Linux from 2008, from Wikimedia Commons. It is not this build and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written and nothing was booted for this page.

shot.alt: Gentoo Linux desktop from 2008 with several terminal windows
shot.caption: Stock screenshot of Gentoo Linux from 2008 · not this build, no image written, no boot tested.

page.status: One image: the amd64 minimal install ISO, written to a USB stick and booted into a shell; the handbook builds the system from there. Writing erases the stick; the install then partitions and formats the target disk.
